svg.text: Co-orbital shepherd mode: fly ahead and below, fire head-on, lower the target's perigee
Not to scale. Earth radius 6,378 km; orbits 750 / 800 km
ablation jet leaves the target at km/s;
a head-on push lowers perigee ~4x more
per m/s than a radial push
after 164 m/s: perigee 200 km, re-entry within weeks
J2 drifts planes 7.9 deg/yr for free
Firing rules (from the article and OrbitFleet)
1 Fire only on targets approaching from ahead:
beam within 60 deg of the target's anti-velocity.
2 Never fire from behind: that raises the orbit.
3 Protected satellites > 0.1 deg off the beam axis
4 Line of sight > 100 km above the Earth limb.
5 Laser sunlit (no pack draw in eclipse).
7 Fine tracker lock confirmed; interlock unit
8 Every shot logged and published per target.
9 Loiter below targets; disposal reserve locked.
Pulse plan vs range (20 J max, 10 Hz, 1 ns, 0.45 m aperture)
Firing time to 200 km perigee from 800 km (98 W on target)
Diffraction-limited spot (2.44 M2 lambda R / D) and optimum-fluence pulse energy
working range 5-12 km: 20 J reaches optimum fluence (26.9 kJ/m2 at 1 ns)
beyond 12 km the 20 J cap leaves fluence below optimum and coupling falls; production unit (700 J, 1 m) works 60-300 km
